answer:
Based on the analysis performed:

**1. Mean slope: 5.75 degrees**

The DEM is in UTM 16N (EPSG:32616), so its 30 m cells are already in meters — no reprojection was needed. Slope was computed using Horn's method (the standard GDAL/ArcGIS algorithm) at the true 30 m resolution. The mean slope is **5.75°** (median 5.82°, std 0.49°). A cross-check with the simple gradient method gave 5.79°, confirming the value.

**2. Watershed area: 16.2 km²**

The outlet at UTM (392265, 4434015) falls at the bottom edge of the DEM (row 199, col 75.5). The DEM is a V-shaped valley with the stream running down column 75; the lowest cell (199,75) at 200.3 m is the natural pour point with the maximum D8 flow accumulation (18,000 cells). Snapping the outlet to this stream cell and tracing the upstream D8 catchment yields **18,000 cells × 900 m² = 16.2 km²** — the full valley watershed (60% of the DEM, spanning rows 80–199 across all columns). The catchment size exactly matches the outlet's flow accumulation (18,000), confirming internal consistency.
